projects.name: Atlas Inference Engine

131 tok/s single-stream on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B with MTP speculative decoding on one DGX Spark
MLPerf Inference v6.1 submitted, closed edge division, on NVIDIA GB10 and AMD Strix Halo from the same CUDA source

32 model recipes across Qwen, Gemma, Nemotron, Mistral, MiniMax and DeepSeek, with multi-node expert parallelism over RoCEv2

projects.name: The Citadel Protocol
projects.description: A post-quantum secure networking protocol and SDK that makes building hyper-secure client-server and peer-to-peer applications easy. Written in 100% safe Rust on Tokio, it provides built-in NAT traversal, post-quantum key exchange (Kyber and NTRU), multi-layered encryption with the patented 3D-matrix ratchet, and a Remote Encrypted Virtual Filesystem, with a very low memory footprint.
highlights: Post-quantum key exchange with Kyber (default) and NTRU; AES-256-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305 and Ascon-80pq ciphers
Patented 3D-matrix ratcheting with per-message re-keying and a true perfect-forward-secrecy mode (US 12,224,993)
Client-server and P2P with built-in NAT traversal (STUN/TURN), over TCP, TLS or QUIC, with optional WebRTC compatibility
Remote Encrypted Virtual Filesystem, device- and credential-based authentication, automatic peer discovery
Filesystem, Redis, MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQLite backends; single- and multi-threaded runtimes; Linux, macOS, Windows, iOS and Android
17-crate workspace; MIT or Apache-2.0 licensed

projects.name: Citadel Workspace
projects.description: A collaborative workspace where every message, file and call is encrypted end to end with post-quantum cryptography, and traffic travels directly between people rather than through a server that could read it. Built on The Citadel Protocol: teams chat, call, share files and edit live documents together, with each member running a local agent that keeps keys and plaintext on their own machine.
highlights: End-to-end encrypted direct and group messaging with offline delivery, voice and video calls, and direct file transfer between peers
One-to-one and group calls over WebCodecs in the browser: no SFU, no TURN server, no third party in the media path
Live collaborative documents merged by a CRDT
Post-quantum only: lattice-based key exchange with no classical-only fallback; a local agent (citadeld) holds the keys
Workspaces organised into a tree of offices and rooms with inherited permissions and custom roles; installable as a PWA
Three-tier architecture: React/TypeScript UI, WASM client layer, Rust backend services across a 5-crate workspace and 3 submodules

projects.name: CertifiedCopy
projects.description: CertifiedCopy exports iPhone and Mac text messages to PDF, CSV, JSON or RSMF entirely inside the browser. The SQLite engine, Apple's undocumented typedstream decoder and the PDF renderer are all compiled to WebAssembly and run on the reader's own machine, so nothing is uploaded: there is no server to upload it to. Every export opens with a SHA-256 record of the source file.
highlights: 100% client-side: the parser, the SQLite engine and the PDF renderer are compiled to WebAssembly and run on the reader's machine; the test suite asserts it on every change
Lighthouse 100 on every category, installable as a PWA, works offline; also a signed and notarised native Mac desktop app
Reads a Mac chat.db or finds sms.db inside an iPhone backup automatically; RSMF output validated against Relativity's published schema 2.0.0
SHA-256 certification page, scoped to FRE 902(14) rather than claiming admissibility; optional notary witnessing with passkey or email-link sign-in
Reverse-engineered Apple's typedstream format to 100% fidelity across 19,724 real messages
Free to export with no account; open source under AGPL-3.0

projects.name: LatticeDB
projects.description: A hybrid graph and vector database built in pure Rust that runs in the browser with zero backend: production-grade HNSW vector search and Cypher graph queries from a ~500 KB WebAssembly module, with a Qdrant-compatible REST API and Neo4j-compatible Cypher when served natively.
highlights: HNSW index with SIMD distance kernels, product and scalar quantization; BFS/DFS traversal, Cypher queries and weighted edges
ACID durability with a write-ahead log; ~500 KB WASM, 2.4 MB memory footprint
Browser (WASM SIMD128), Linux x86_64 (AVX2/AVX-512), macOS Apple Silicon (NEON) and Windows x86_64, plus Service Worker and Cloudflare Workers serving
Published benchmark at 1,000 x 128-dim vectors: 84 us in-memory search and 168 us over HTTP against 330 us for Qdrant over HTTP
Powers AutoRepoRAG corpora and the browser-side search planned for GeoHarness

projects.name: GeoHarness
projects.description: A GitHub Action that makes any website agent-ready on Cloudflare's free plan: it builds the site, gives every page a markdown twin served to AI agents on Accept: text/markdown, writes llms.txt, a sitemap and robots.txt Content Signals, gates the build on an evidence-graded GEO score and Lighthouse 100 in all four categories, deploys to Cloudflare Workers or Pages, and verifies the live site with real AI user agents. This site is deployed by it.
highlights: 29 evidence-graded checks in 5 scoring categories (AI access, indexability, markdown delivery, extractability, signals), each cited to a published source
Pure WebAssembly core with no filesystem, network, clock or process access; tools pinned by exact version and inputs passed as environment variables, never a shell

Lighthouse gate: 100 in performance, accessibility, best practices and SEO as the median of 3 runs, locally against the deploy's own wrangler config and again against the live site, with automatic rollback
Live verification with an Accept matrix and eight AI user agents; ACME certificate renewal through Cloudflare DNS-01
Adapters for npm, Vite, SvelteKit, Python, make and static sites

projects.name: AutoRepoRAG
projects.description: A GitHub Action that turns a repository into a ready-to-query vector corpus straight from CI: it chunks the source, embeds it against any OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint (or deterministic mock vectors that need no secrets), loads and verifies every vector against a checksum-pinned LatticeDB server, and exports a byte-deterministic corpus that a browser, a bot or another pipeline can load directly.
highlights: Zero npm dependencies, no Docker, no build step: a composite action running vendored Node ESM
Verifies point counts, self-retrieval and scroll fidelity against the live index before exporting
Byte-deterministic lattice-jsonl corpus with a gzip twin and a metadata manifest
Every input that shapes the corpus is required and has no default

projects.name: synchronized.work
projects.description: Cross-person coordination for coding agents: one live tree of projects, tasks, people, agents and progress, with post-quantum signed prompts and Sign in with Citadel. Rust compiled to WebAssembly on Cloudflare Workers, with the Citadel Protocol as its transport.
highlights: Agents join the tree through an MCP server; a remote prompt reaches an agent only if it is signed with ML-DSA-65
One live tree, Project > Task > Person > Agent > Progress, with cooperation tiers off, aware and synchronized
Sealed messages use ML-KEM-768 with HKDF-SHA3-256 and AES-256-GCM
Rust and WebAssembly on Cloudflare Workers; MIT or Apache-2.0 licensed
